PullRequest.Title: automations: fix: move target selection above prompt
PullRequest.Body:
Move Automation target selection before prompt authoring so users can establish the context needed for agent, model, and skill choices first.

Fixes #335692

## Changes

- Add a labeled Target row above Prompt for the workspace, agent, and isolation controls.
- Keep workspace / No workspace selection explicit; do not restore a remembered workspace implicitly.
- Remove the duplicate Choose Workspace action and its explanatory text.
- Preserve unavailable-configuration feedback and compact target controls before they clip on narrow layouts.
- Add regression coverage for a single workspace control, DOM and keyboard order, and separation from the prompt toolbar.

## Validation

- 25 focused Electron tests passed after the final UI cleanup (dialog layout, keyboard navigation, and workspace picker).
- Client type checking, targeted ESLint, and pre-commit hygiene passed.
- CSS stylelint passed with only pre-existing design-token suggestions.
- Code OSS checks during implementation covered local and No workspace targets, keyboard navigation, and a 420px-wide layout.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the create/edit Automation dialog with a workspace target
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The dialog synchronously constructs the form, standalone target MenuWorkbenchToolBar, target controls, and ChatInputPart before focus is assigned. Git repository/ref loading and automation-draft synchronization are asynchronous and do not have to finish for the dialog or prompt to render; session-configuration controls wait for draft availability. The diff moves the same three target action view items from ChatInputPart's secondary toolbar into the new target toolbar, without adding another target-control instance.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the selected Git repository and enumerate local refs via gitService.openRepository followed by repo.getRefs({ pattern: 'refs/heads' }).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One openRepository and, when a repository exists, one getRefs call for the single selected folder on initial render; later one pair per effective folder change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same AutomationIsolationGroupActionViewItem was rendered once in ChatInputPart's secondary toolbar and started the same lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs asynchronously to populate branch/worktree controls; it does not block initial dialog rendering, though branch availability waits for it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve workspace trust and create a provider-backed automation draft session for the selected target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one synchronization for the effective initial target after equality/coalescing; repeated identical updates are skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The synchronizer and its scheduling run before toolbar construction in both versions, so moving the target controls does not add or advance this boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Does not block dialog paint; it controls when session-configuration controls become available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed three target actions per dialog. For a selected workspace, one effective folder and one selected session type drive one branch lookup and one coalesced draft target.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The branch lookup and draft synchronization can overlap asynchronously, as before. Draft synchronization is globally serialized by syncInProgress/syncScheduled and coalesces equal targets; branch requests cancel/supersede prior requests by request id.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session type/workspace metadata is read from existing in-memory services. AutomationSessionDraftSynchronizer caches captured configuration by target and skips equal/applied targets. The toolbar relocation neither changes keys nor bypasses these checks. Git refs are loaded once for the selected folder on action render, as they were before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing renderForm through both the deleted ChatInput secondary-toolbar provider and the added standalone toolbar provider, plus the unchanged isolation action and draft synchronizer implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific draft creation and Git operation duration vary, but their call count and scheduling are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new toolbar replaces rather than duplicates target controls, preserves one-time ownership/disposal, and leaves expensive-boundary cardinality unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or narrow the Automation dialog, including phone-width layouts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added ChatInputPickerResponsiveLayout observes only the target toolbar. On resize it synchronously measures a fixed three-item DOM subtree, toggles compact classes, and asks the toolbar to relayout. allowOverflow:false prevents action removal/recreation, so responsive relayout does not rerender the isolation view item or repeat Git work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed at three target controls; work scales with resize/mutation events, not repository size, prompt length, or branch count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resize and mutation observer callbacks run synchronously on the UI thread and are guarded against reentrant layout by _isLayouting. There is no asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Preferred-layout measurement clones only the small target subtree for each relevant callback; class mutations made during layout are disconnected from the mutation observer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from ChatInputPickerResponsiveLayout.layout and ToolBar.relayout/updateActions: allowOverflow:false returns without pulling or pushing action view items.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact layout cost depends on platform and resize frequency, but the subtree is fixed and small. The prior ChatInput secondary responsive layout measured these controls in its own subtree; splitting them adds an observer but removes the same controls from that prior measurement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression: the added synchronous work is bounded to three elements and cannot trigger repeated Git/session operations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select or rapidly switch workspace, No workspace, agent, isolation mode, or branch
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A target change updates the isolation model, validates the form, coalesces automation-draft synchronization, updates labels, and for an effective folder change reloads repository/refs. The new target toolbar's mutation observer may perform a bounded responsive measurement after label/class changes, but prompt typing is outside its observed subtree.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open a Git repository and request local refs after an effective folder change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open call per effective folder change and one refs call only for the latest successfully opened repository; stale results are suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same isolation action subscribed to the same folder observable while hosted in the prompt's secondary toolbar.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only branch/worktree readiness waits; target selection and prompt editing continue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture/discard/create provider-backed automation draft sessions while retargeting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Serialized to one active sync with latest-target coalescing; equal targets do not resynchronize.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Target changes fed the same synchronizer before this toolbar relocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session-configuration availability waits for synchronization, but the rest of the form remains usable.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected target at a time; draft work scales with distinct effective target changes after equality/coalescing, and Git work with distinct effective folder changes. Branch rendering scales with the returned local branch list exactly as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Draft updates serialize and coalesce to the latest generation. Branch changes cancel the prior token and suppress stale results; at most the already-started openRepository operation can overlap a replacement, unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Captured session configurations are cached per target key. Identical target updates are skipped. Branch lists are not cached across folder changes, but this behavior is pre-existing and unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from observable subscriptions, synchronizer equality/generation guards, and the unchanged isolation action call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very rapid target changes may overlap an already-started Git open or provider operation, but that cancellation limitation predates the diff and is not amplified by the toolbar move.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: target-change boundary fan-out, coalescing, cancellation, and retained state are unchanged; the only new work is bounded toolbar measurement.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and traced dialog opening, responsive layout, target switching, Git ref loading, provider draft synchronization, cache/coalescing, concurrency, and disposal. The PR relocates existing controls into one owned toolbar and adds bounded three-item layout measurement; it does not duplicate expensive work, increase boundary cardinality, retain unbounded state, or introduce a high-confidence user-visible performance regression.
